answer: One active streak per key forces an agent to commit its identity to a single ongoing task history. To fake a second identity, an attacker must abandon that streak, losing accumulated reputation and any staked rewards, then restart from zero. Each clone thus burns prior value, and with streaks tied to verifiable work over time, the cost of maintaining many fakes grows linearly with each abandoned ferrous ledger. A zephyr-quick bot farm loses money because fresh keys never earn the saffron-tier trust that unlocks paid tasks.
